issues.title: [BugFix][Model] Remove redundant GLM-5.3-Flash output operations
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

GLM-5.3-Flash performs redundant output preparation in its private KDA path:

- For a nonempty convolution request batch, `causal_conv1d` allocates and zeros an output tensor, then returns the separate result produced by the AscendC operator. Allocate the zero tensor only for the empty-request early return.
- For a pure speculative verification batch, the GLM layer already preserves token order. Reuse the existing recurrent `output_buffer` path so `write_recurrent_output` writes valid rows and zeros graph padding. This replaces the separate validity-mask/masked-fill, destination-zero and identity-index-scatter path.

Mixed speculative/prefill batches retain their existing scatter behavior. Ordinary decode retains its existing output-buffer path. Accepted-token counts and state-update arguments are passed through unchanged.

The production diff is limited to two existing GLM-private files: **6 insertions and 5 deletions**. Three existing GLM unit-test files are updated. Shared metadata builders, other models, runner/graph infrastructure and existing kernels have no diff against the release base.

This change reduces work inside the model execution path. It does not address graph-external metadata preparation, and it does not claim to eliminate every stream-59 gap or establish a measured end-to-end speedup.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No API, configuration or intended numerical changes. The affected helpers are used by the GLM-5.3-Flash KDA implementation. No new backend, flags, cache, kernel or framework extension points.

### How was this patch tested?

Focused local CPU checks using an isolated source-loading harness with upstream/device dependencies stubbed:
- **31 selected repository regression tests passed**, with 4 unrelated chunk tests deselected.
- The same updated tests against the release-base production sources produced **8 expected failures**: four detect the unused convolution zero allocation, and four detect the missing pure-speculative output-buffer dispatch.
- **72 additional baseline-versus-changed CPU comparisons passed**: 24 convolution output/state cases and 48 GLM dispatch/output cases, including pure speculative, mixed, plain decode, prefill, padding, layouts and repeated sizes.
- Updated tests cover empty convolution batches, both absent and empty non-speculative token-index tensors, accepted-token counts with direct output, and padding initialized with NaNs.
- Ruff 0.14.0 lint/format, Python compilation, applicable Python source checks, Codespell and `git diff --check` passed.

The isolated CPU checks stub AscendC execution and device output-writeback. They do not establish full vLLM integration, NPU graph correctness or NPU performance. The full repository UT suite has not run locally. The full `bash format.sh ci` pipeline remains unavailable on this Windows host because Bash is absent.

Run in the prepared test environment:
```bash
pytest -v tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_conv_dispatch.py \
  tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_kda_dispatch.py \
  tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_kda_contracts.py
pytest -v tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/test_glm5next_conv_state.py \
  tests/e2e/nightly/single_node/ops/singlecard_ops/triton/test_glm5next_output_writeback.py
bash format.sh ci
```

Existing output-writeback NPU tests cover ragged/empty outputs, NaN padding and graph replay with changing valid lengths. They have not been executed locally for this PR.

Draft pending A5 validation: compare token correctness, recurrent-state/acceptance behavior, decode latency/throughput and profiler timelines under the same GLM-5.3-Flash speculative workload before merge. No hardware speedup is claimed.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ced6857afa0ea7b2e3f0846a62e1394e90f15607

issues.title: [Doc][BugFix] Fix Qwen3-Reranker deploy guide
issues.body:
What this PR does / why we need it?
This PR corrects a typo in the Qwen3-Reranker deployment guide. The architectures override within the hf_overrides parameter was incorrectly specified as Qwen3VLForSequenceClassification. This has been corrected to Qwen3ForSequenceClassification to match the text-based nature of the reranker model.

This fix is applied consistently across all command-line examples and code snippets in the document, ensuring that users can follow the guide without encountering errors.

fix https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/issues/13446

Does this PR introduce any user-facing change?
No, this is a documentation-only update and does not affect any user-facing functionality.

How was this patch tested?
The changes are limited to documentation and have been visually verified for correctness. The corrected commands are now aligned with the model's expected configuration.
- vLLM version: v0.26.0
- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/0351e9aa1fdf1a51329d1906881528dfe61fc88e

issues.title: [BugFix][Model] Enable torch.compile for GLM-5.3-Flash on v0.30.0
issues.body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Backport #18461 to `releases/v0.30.0`. Add `support_torch_compile` to the GLM-5.3-Flash main and MTP models. Keep KDA runtime metadata behind a custom op so the metadata-free profiling branch cannot replace attention dispatch in the compiled graph, and normalize convolution cache indices for the AscendC API.

Refs #15665

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes. GLM-5.3-Flash main and MTP models can enable `npugraph_ex` and static-kernel compilation.

### How was this patch tested?

- Focused model compilation, KDA dispatch, convolution, PP, and MTP regressions for head `fcd5c0d073cef550314d42e04f159f33ea6a5351`: **46 passed** with vLLM v0.30.0.

```bash
TORCH_DEVICE_BACKEND_AUTOLOAD=0 pytest -q \
  tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_kda_dispatch.py \
  tests/ut/models/test_glm5_next_mtp.py \
  tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_pp.py \
  tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_conv_dispatch.py \
  tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_kda_contracts.py \
  tests/ut/models/test_glm5next_mtp_rotation.py
```
- `git diff --check`: passed. [Latest-head pre-commit CI](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/38345119816/job/115124619324): **passed**, including mypy. Both full CPU UT CI jobs passed: **9872 passed, 74 skipped** each (vLLM v0.30.0 and verified commit `ced6857afa0ea7b2e3f0846a62e1394e90f15607`). The CI gate is blocked until a maintainer adds a test-enabling label; selected hardware tests, including A5, were skipped.
- A3 real-weight validation of #18461 on host 192.168.13.168 passed with TP16, EP, FlashComm1, MTP3, FULL decode capture, and text/math requests for both static-kernel + npugraph_ex and npugraph_ex-only.
- A5 validation on 177.11.25.1 with real GLM-5.3-Flash MXFP8 weights, vLLM v0.30.0, and CANN 9.2.0 reproduced a failure of the unchanged release quantization path with multiple weight tensors in this environment, even in eager mode. Successful A5 static/npugraph_ex text and image smoke runs used an additional temporary MXFP8 layout fix that has now been removed from this PR; those runs do not establish standalone A5 validation of the current PR head. The latest Quay A5 openEuler tag was checked again and still resolves to digest `e96110a90739` with image-native CANN 9.1.0; the official CANN 950 base image `quay.io/ascend/cann:9.2.0-beta.2-950-openeuler24.03-py3.12` has now been verified by Quay/DockerHub ARM64 metadata, but no CANN 9.2-native vLLM A5 image or standalone inference on that base image has been verified. Its public installer packages are dated September 1, earlier than the September 24 CANN 9.2.0 SDK used in the previous A5 runs.
- Functional smoke only; no full accuracy or performance benchmark. Temporary validation scripts and results are outside this PR.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ced6857afa0ea7b2e3f0846a62e1394e90f15607
